review.rationale: Three complete scientific prompt bodies (14,870 bytes), two assigned whole native PNGs and two associated whole native v2 PNGs were freshly read/viewed, with both complete pinned parent versions. Eighteen frozen units comprise 13 canonical teaching requirements (11 current root representations and2 actual unmerged definition dependencies) and 5 authored-convention checks without canonical-coverage credit. Two construction rows remain partial: the old wrong Target leaders in both legacy images and the distinct blank assay display not clearly visible in v2. The pinned parent uses v2, not either assigned legacy PNG. Eighteen exact excerpts occur in 4 actual root and 2 separate actual-peer EntityDetail renders. Five complete abstracts,6 selected FDA body pages and selected NCI paragraphs retain their actual depth; no whole-paper or whole-guidance claim. No canonical, component, alias, relation, reviewer-stamp or artwork edits. No independent, expert, owner, learner, native-language, hosted/browser, hydration or accessibility acceptance.

points.requirement: Recognition is one part of a therapeutic design; connected formats add separate actions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A recognition molecule can be used as one component of a larger therapeutic design. Its ability to bind is one property of that component.
evidence.explanation: The dedicated unmerged binder owner supplies the generic component definition; a modality record is not substituted for that owner. Watson is a complete abstract about designed protein binders; Eshhar is a complete abstract about an experimental scFv receptor in a T-cell hybridoma. The generic component definition is a scoped synthesis, not a new clinical result. The dedicated definition remains an actual unmerged PR373 dependency, not a root integration.

points.requirement: The binder and the molecular target it contacts are distinct objects; purple and blue are drawing conventions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The antibody recognizes an accessible antigen; the attachment chemistry and linker affect stability and release; the payload acts through its own molecular mechanism.
evidence.explanation: Recognition and the recognized antigen are separate objects in the current ADC mechanism. The purple/blue labels remain a separately checked drawing choice. The FDA ADC selected pages describe antibody/fragment, linker and payload in cytotoxic conjugates. They do not cover every therapeutic cargo. Purple and blue are authored identifiers, not molecular properties. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: An accessible intended target can occur on cancer and healthy cells; recognition alone gives no tumour exclusivity or safety conclusion.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Healthy tissues can carry either recognized target
evidence.explanation: The current bispecific owner explicitly carries recognized targets on healthy tissue, with no safety conclusion from specificity alone. The selected NCI paragraphs name CD20 on B cells and some cancer cells in its rituximab example. This supports possible shared recognition, not a statement that every cancer antigen is equally accessible on all healthy cells. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Linking chemical cargo to recognition does not by itself establish entry, processing or usable payload at its action site.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding can support delivery, but uptake, processing, access to the payload’s target and cellular response require separate evidence.
evidence.explanation: Binding, uptake, processing, action-site access and response remain separate. FDA ADC printed pages 1 to 3 describe distinct constituent parts, release mechanisms and exposure considerations. The separate-test reading rule does not assume that every conjugate follows one guaranteed route. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The illustrated soluble T-cell engager has distinct target-recognition and CD3-recognition arms binding different features on separate cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: CD20/CD3 lymphoma engagers illustrate one bispecific format: CD20 recognition connects to T-cell recruitment through CD3.
evidence.explanation: The named CD20/CD3 example and two linked scFv architecture jointly carry the illustrated distinct binding functions. Mack is one experimental construct, not a universal topology for every engager. Mack describes two scFv fragments joined by a peptide linker, one directed at CD3 and the other at epithelial 17-1A. The NCI paragraph gives a separate named CD19/CD3 example. These are illustrative architectures, not all engager forms. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The Mack construct joined two single-chain Fv fragments with a peptide linker in one compact protein; this is different from an IgG architecture with an Fc region.
evidence.explanation: The named CD20/CD3 example and two linked scFv architecture jointly carry the illustrated distinct binding functions. Mack is one experimental construct, not a universal topology for every engager. Mack describes two scFv fragments joined by a peptide linker, one directed at CD3 and the other at epithelial 17-1A. The NCI paragraph gives a separate named CD19/CD3 example. These are illustrative architectures, not all engager forms. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: Bridging contact alone is not evidence of productive activation or target killing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: T-cell engagers are proteins that bind a specified target and recruit T cells, often through CD3. A binding bridge does not by itself establish completed killing.
evidence.explanation: The registered engager TLDR explicitly withholds completed killing from a binding bridge. Mack measured cytotoxicity separately from binding. Bluemel reports different lysis despite similar target affinity in engineered CHO systems. The no-guarantee reading rule is an inference about evidence, not a new failure frequency. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: The cell-receptor example spans the T-cell membrane and links extracellular recognition to an intracellular signalling design.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region.
evidence.explanation: The registered CAR principle carries external recognition, transmembrane linkage and internal signalling. Eshhar used anti-trinitrophenyl scFv linked to gamma or zeta signalling chains in a cytolytic T-cell hybridoma. The selected FDA CAR guidance concerns ex vivo manufactured products and separates recognition from signalling. Neither supplies a general clinical outcome. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

points.requirement: A living-cell receptor and a soluble bridging protein are different formats; a floating antibody is not itself a cell receptor.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A dosed T-cell engager supplies a protein connecting target recognition to an available T cell. It does not itself install receptor instructions or supply engineered living responders.
evidence.explanation: The protein engager and receptor-bearing living cell are explicitly different administered/design objects. Mack concerns an expressed soluble bispecific protein; Eshhar concerns functional surface receptors in a cellular model. The FDA guidance discusses a living, genetically modified cell product. These object distinctions do not establish comparative efficacy. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects.

points.requirement: Function of the assembled product needs testing; receptor anatomy or a signalling symbol is not a measured successful response.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts.
evidence.explanation: Readouts and the schematic response arrow are explicitly separated from demonstrated expression or completed killing. Eshhar measured IL2 secretion and lysis in a defined model. A drawn signalling ray is not one of these measurements. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.
evidence.explanation: Readouts and the schematic response arrow are explicitly separated from demonstrated expression or completed killing. The separate-question rule supplies no patient-benefit estimate. Current registered local-root field; not main or live acceptance.
